ma.navigateToMiniProgram(Object object)

Jump to other Mini Programs within a Mini Program (minimum version: 23.12.0)

When allowing the opening of Mini Programs, parameters can be carried and passed by concatenating them into a format like index.html?paramA=xxx&paramB=xxxx (changed in version 25.12.0). Only H5 Mini Programs are supported; DSL Mini Programs are not supported. The following special characters are not allowed: Double dots:.. Dot-slash:./ Cross-directory file separator:..\ and %00

Parameter

Object object

Attribute Type Default Value Mandatory or Not Description
appId String Yes The appId of the Mini Program to be opened
capsuleShow Boolean true Yes Whether the capsule is visible
path String No The path of the page to open. If it is empty, the home page will be opened.
params Object No When navigating to other mini-programs, parameters should be passed in the form of paramA=xxx&paramB=xxx (only supports H5 mini-programs, minimum version: 25.12.0)
success Function No Callback function for a successful API call.
fail Function No Callback function for a failed API call.
complete Function No Callback function used when an API call is complete. (This callback function is used regardless of whether the API call succeeds or fails.)

object.fail Callback Function

Parameter

Object res

Attribute Type Description
errMsg String error message
errno Integer error code

Error Code List

Error Scenario Error Code Supported by Android Supported by iOS Supported by Simulator Development Suggestion
Invalid request parameter type. 1 Yes Yes Yes Check whether the parameter type in the interface invoking parameter is valid based on errorMsg.
Invalid request parameter value. 2 Yes Yes Yes Check whether the parameter value in the interface invoking parameter is valid based on errorMsg.
The request parameter is not mandatory. 3 Yes Yes Yes Check which mandatory parameters are not specified in the interface invoking parameters based on errorMsg.
Failed to query the Mini Program based on appId in the request. 203000 Yes Yes No Check whether the Mini Program to be redirected has a running version based on the input parameter appId.
The user cancels the redirection to the specified Mini Program pop-up window. 203001 Yes Yes No Developer-friendly implementation, prompting the user to manually confirm when opening the associated Mini Program.
Failed to open the Mini Program to be redirected to. 203002 Yes Yes No Contact the current site operation personnel to locate the cause of the failure to open the Mini Program.
Request parameters contain invalid strings. 203003 Yes Yes No Check whether the params in the interface call parameters are valid according to errorMsg.
No response when redirecting to other mini-programs 203004 No Yes No Contact the current site's operations staff to coordinate with the host app developer to determine the reason why the mini-program is not responding when redirected.

Sample Code

ma.navigateToMiniProgram({
  appId: '', 
    capsuleShow: false,
  path: 'page/index/index',
  success: (res) => {
  },
  fail: (res) => {
  },
  complete: (res) => {
  }
});

Usage Restrictions

  1. To use this interface, you need to connect to the Mini Program SaaS platform

Tips

  1. Note that this API needs to invoke the server interface to query and download Mini Program. Therefore, user operations must be shielded during API invoking to avoid unknown problems. trustlist is configured on the Mini Program SaaS platform. After authorization, no pop-up window is displayed asking whether to jump to another Mini Program. Instead, other Mini Programs are directly opened.
  2. In the scenario where the Mini Program is redirected through navigateToMiniProgram, the latest version of the Mini Program is queried by default. There is no upgrade experience scenario, for example, a pop-up window prompting the upgrade is displayed.
